description_full: F5, Inc. provides multi-cloud application security and delivery solutions in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific region. The company's distributed cloud services enable its customers to deploy, secure, and operate applications in architecture, from on-premises to the public cloud. It also offers unified, security, networking, and application management solutions, such as web app and API protection; multi-cloud networking; application delivery and deployment; domain name system; content delivery network; and application deployment and orchestration. In addition, the company provides application security and delivery products, including NGINX Plus; NGINX One Console; NGINX Ingress Controller; WAF for NGINX; BIG-IP Packaged Software; and BIG-IP Systems. Further, it provides a range of professional services, including maintenance, consulting, training, and other technical support services. The company sells its products to large enterprise businesses, public sector institutions, governments, and service providers through distributors, value-added resellers, managed service providers, systems integrators, and other indirect channel partners. It has partnerships with public cloud providers, such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform. The company was formerly known as F5 Networks, Inc. and changed its name to F5, Inc. in November 2021. F5, Inc. was incorporated in 1996 and is headquartered in Seattle, Washington.

financial_summary: F5, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $17.3B market cap on $3.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 26% against a 10% cost of capital — a 17-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 82% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $869M in free cash flow — roughly 25 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.33× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.5% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 102% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 16% over the last three months.

Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 5.0% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.9% (vs the 8% bar).

prof: ROIC of 26% clears the cost of capital of 9.9% by 17pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.93).
It runs a 82% gross margin and converts 25% of revenue into free cash flow, or 18% after stock compensation.

ROE of 18% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.3B.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 5.3, in the safe zone).

Goodwill makes up 35% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 6.7% over 3 years, 5.6% over 5 years and 5.5% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 61% of profits supports about 16.2% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 7.2% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.06 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 64% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 10%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 2.7% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 23, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.6%), and institutions hold 99%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (38 sales, net $9.3M sold).
It returns 3.5% a year to shareholders (3.5% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 1.3% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 6,632 employees, each generates about $515K of revenue, 1.4x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 8.8% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $131K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.4M (5x revenue per employee).
